title.narrative: Activity under preparation CSO - mining Governance

description.narrative: Contract related to: CSO - mining Governance - After the 2021 general elections in Zambia, a new administration was elected, under the leadership of President Hakainde Hichilema. The ¿new dawn¿ Government has expressed strong commitment to reforming the public administration, fighting corruption and upholding the rule of law. The proposed Action aims at supporting the Government to implement its planned PFM Reform Strategy, its Revenue Action Plan, and develop its Medium-Term Revenue Strategy, aiming at restoring fiscal sustainability and improving efficiency and effectiveness of public resource allocation, and spending, for better public service delivery. This will help the country achieve its national development objectives. The Action will also aim at supporting the national accountability system and assist the Government in fighting corruption. In this context, we propose to structure the Action around the following two components:·  Component 1: Public revenue and expenditure management. The Action will support the Government to implement its PFM Reform Strategy, with an emphasis on outputs, aiming at strengthening budget credibility. The action will aim at ensuring reliable provision of domestic funding for public service delivery in the social sectors. This includes strengthening transparency and accountability in budget planning and execution. In addition, the Action will continue to support the Government to collect domestic revenues more efficiently, by assisting in the design of effective, gender responsive, environmentally and socially responsible domestic revenue mobilization policies. The component will also strengthen the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Finance and National Planning (MoFNP) and other core PFM actors to deliver on their mandate with a focus on change management to implement strategic PFM reforms.·  Component 2: Transparency and accountability. The Action will strengthen the national accountability system by enhancing transparent handling of funds, legislative oversight and external scrutiny of the Government¿s operations. The Action will also support Government¿s pledge to a zero-tolerance for corruption, and to uphold the independence of the institutions mandated to investigate and prosecute corruption cases.The Action will mainstream human rights, democracy and gender equality as cross-cutting issues. It will engage with state and non-state actors. A particular focus will be on empowering civil society to enhance its role in the national accountability system. The Action further aims at improving the climate responsiveness of the PFM systems, in view of Zambia¿s commitment to climate actions, enshrined in its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.
